text: Second timeline branch in a day, and this one is back to year 11,900. The year-14,500 restore died at about year 14,791, and the original timeline died from that same checkpoint at 14,845: two independent runs from one state, both dead inside three hundred years, which means that population was already dying when I restored it. It was not food, not toxins and not the repro_threshold ratchet. Health held at 0.97 to 0.99, animals kept 97 to 99 per cent of the energy in what they ate, and the breeding bar fell rather than rose. It was geography. In every healthy archive, 53 to 67 per cent of all the world's harvestable food lay within twelve cells of some animal. In the restored run that fell to 11.6 per cent and then 3.3, while the number of rich cells went from 270 to 5,115. The flora bloomed across the map and the animals never went to it. They could not see it: sense radius is 1 + sense_range x 12 cells, sense_range had evolved down to 0.193, about three cells, and the nearest rich cell was a median seven away. Sensing costs upkeep, so short sight pays while food is underfoot and becomes a trap once the local patch is grazed out. The year-14,500 population was already contracted -- 270 rich cells, median distance 7.1 -- and so were its descendants, both times. Year 11,900 is the healthiest state with the most room: 391 animals, 15.3 per cent land against the 10 it has eroded to since, two thirds of the food within reach, stable for centuries, and from before spikes existed. It carries only the two laws it lived under for millennia, trait_cost_scale 0.25 and growth_scale 0.13. I have not re-applied the carnivory fix: that subsidy only ever proved lethal in worlds I seeded by hand, and this evolved world ran predator-prey cycles under it for nearly two thousand years. Everything between 11,900 and 15,041 is kept -- the dead state as archive/pre-restore-dead-world-y15041, the earlier one as pre-restore-dead-world-y19490, and every Chronicle entry from both rewound timelines. Separately, the power cut on 2026-09-13 left 1,152 NUL bytes in chronicle.jsonl and 841 in chronicle.md at the exact instant of shutdown; they are stripped, backups kept, and all 167,634 lines parse.
